title: Studying hospitality management in Germany
description: Where to study hospitality and tourism management in Germany, in English or German, what the degrees involve and which careers follow.
html:
Germany is not the first country most people associate with hospitality education, but its hotel industry, trade fair sector and tourism economy are among the largest in Europe, and several universities offer well-regarded programmes, many in English.

Why Germany

Low or no tuition at public institutions, a large hotel and events industry for internships, a central location for travel across Europe and the same 18-month post-study work permit that every graduate receives.

English-taught programmes

Most English-taught hospitality programmes are at universities of applied sciences and private hotel schools. Bachelor's programmes typically run three to four years with one or two compulsory internship semesters; master's programmes take one to two years and often combine hospitality with general management or tourism.

Where to study

Hotel management schools in Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg have long traditions and close ties to luxury hotel groups. Universities of applied sciences in Munich, Heilbronn, Kempten and Worms offer international tourism and hospitality programmes. A few private universities in Berlin and Hamburg add an international business angle.

What the degrees cover

Hotel operations, food and beverage management, revenue management, marketing, finance and human resources, plus tourism economics and, increasingly, sustainability and digital tools. Practical semesters in hotels or event companies are standard.

Related fields

Tourism management, event management, international business with a service focus, and culinary management all lead into similar careers with a different emphasis.

Frequently asked questions

Is German required? Not for English-taught programmes, but it is a major advantage in the industry. What are the admission requirements? A recognised school-leaving certificate, an English certificate and sometimes an interview. What do graduates earn? Entry-level salaries in hotel management sit around €35,000 to €45,000, rising with responsibility and with a move into corporate roles.
